items.followUp: State Newton’s Third Law of Motion and explain it using the example of a swimmer moving forward.

rubric.why: The law requires the action and reaction forces to be equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.
rubric.description: States Newton’s Third Law of Motion.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks when the answer identifies action and reaction as equal and opposite.

rubric.why: This identifies the swimmer’s action on the water.
rubric.description: Explains that the swimmer pushes the water backward.
rubric.how: Look for the swimmer exerting a backward force on the water.

rubric.why: This identifies the reaction force that moves the swimmer forward.
rubric.description: Explains that the water pushes the swimmer forward.
rubric.how: Look for the water exerting a forward force on the swimmer.

modelAnswer: Newton’s Third Law of Motion states: For every action, there is an equal and opposite reaction.
A swimmer pushes the water backward with their hands and feet; this is the action.
The water pushes the swimmer forward with an equal and opposite force; this is the reaction.
The swimmer moves forward as a result.
